from solution import solve


def test_issue_example_given():
    """Example asserts solve([1,0,2],3) == True."""
    # pairs: (1,0) global+local, (1,2) none, (0,2) none => global=1 local=1 => True
    assert solve([1, 0, 2], 3) == True


def test_issue_sorted_has_no_inversions():
    """Ideal sorted input has equal (zero) global and local counts."""
    # pairs: (0,1) none, (0,2) none, (1,2) none => global=0 local=0 => True
    assert solve([0, 1, 2], 3) == True


def test_issue_adjacent_swap_at_end():
    """One adjacent swap still has equal global and local counts."""
    # pairs: (0,2) none, (0,1) none, (2,1) global+local => global=1 local=1 => True
    assert solve([0, 2, 1], 3) == True


def test_issue_distant_inversion_is_not_ideal():
    """A value moved two positions makes global and local counts differ."""
    # pairs: (1,2) none, (1,0) global, (2,0) global+local => global=2 local=1 => False
    assert solve([1, 2, 0], 3) == False


def test_issue_fully_reversed_three():
    """Reversed triple has more global than local inversions."""
    # pairs: (2,1) global+local, (2,0) global, (1,0) global+local => global=3 local=2 => False
    assert solve([2, 1, 0], 3) == False


def test_issue_empty_input():
    """Empty input has zero inversions of both types."""
    # pairs: none => global=0 local=0 => True
    assert solve([], 0) == True


def test_issue_single_element():
    """Single element has zero inversions of both types."""
    # pairs: none => global=0 local=0 => True
    assert solve([0], 1) == True


def test_issue_two_sorted():
    """Two sorted elements have zero inversions of both types."""
    # pairs: (0,1) none => global=0 local=0 => True
    assert solve([0, 1], 2) == True


def test_issue_two_reversed():
    """Two reversed elements have one global and one local inversion."""
    # pairs: (1,0) global+local => global=1 local=1 => True
    assert solve([1, 0], 2) == True


def test_issue_two_disjoint_adjacent_swaps():
    """Two disjoint adjacent swaps keep global and local counts equal."""
    # globals: (1,0) yes + (3,2) yes = 2; locals: 1>0 yes, 0>3 no, 3>2 yes = 2 => True
    assert solve([1, 0, 3, 2], 4) == True


def test_contract_returns_bool():
    """Example uses '== True' so solve returns bool."""
    # pairs: (1,0) global+local, (1,2) none, (0,2) none => global=1 local=1 => True
    result = solve([1, 0, 2], 3)
    assert result is True


def test_contract_repeated_calls_stable():
    """Pure function gives same result on repeated calls."""
    # pairs: (1,2) none, (1,0) global, (2,0) global+local => global=2 local=1 => False
    assert solve([1, 2, 0], 3) == False
    # same arithmetic again => False
    assert solve([1, 2, 0], 3) == False
